# pantechdynamics_dynamic_ip (Resource)

Dynamic IP for a running standard instance: outbound traffic leaves from a public IPv4 address that rotates on the chosen schedule, while inbound traffic continues to reach the instance's static address. Requires a standard instance (not in a VPC subnet) running a supported image with the platform agent and a security group whose inbound rules exclude the zone's private network. While enabled, a schedule surcharge is added to the instance's hourly price: every_12_hours (+60%), daily (+50%), weekly (+40%), or monthly (+30%). Changes to schedule, connections, and on_demand apply in place without replacing the instance. Do not manage Dynamic IP for the same instance with both this resource and pantechdynamics_instance.dynamic_ip.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Enable Dynamic IP on a running standard instance. Outbound traffic leaves from
# a rotating public IPv4 address while inbound traffic continues to reach the
# instance's static address.
resource "pantechdynamics_dynamic_ip" "worker" {
  instance_id = pantechdynamics_instance.worker.id
  schedule    = "daily" # every_12_hours, daily, weekly, or monthly
  connections = "keep"  # keep (default) or move
  on_demand   = false   # requires on-demand rotation enabled for your organization
}

output "worker_outbound_ip" {
  value = pantechdynamics_dynamic_ip.worker.current_address
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) Id of the instance to enable Dynamic IP on, starting with vm_. Changing it replaces this resource.
- `schedule` (String) How often the outbound public address rotates: "every_12_hours", "daily", "weekly", or "monthly". Changes in place.

### Optional

- `connections` (String) How existing outbound connections behave on rotation: "keep" (default) lets open connections finish on the previous address; "move" switches them to the new address immediately. Changes in place.
- `on_demand` (Boolean) Whether on-demand rotation is allowed for this instance. Requires on-demand rotation to be enabled for your organization. Defaults to false. Changes in place.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `current_address` (String) The rotating public IPv4 address the instance currently uses for outbound traffic, or null before the first address is ready or while falling back to the instance's own address.
- `failure_reason` (String) Explanation when state is "failed" or "degraded", or null otherwise.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the Dynamic IP configuration, equal to instance_id.
- `last_rotated_at` (String) When the outbound address last rotated, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `next_rotation_at` (String) When the next scheduled rotation is due, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `on_demand_limit` (Number) Maximum number of on-demand rotations allowed per 24 hours.
- `on_demand_used` (Number) Number of on-demand rotations performed in the last 24 hours.
- `state` (String) Current lifecycle state of Dynamic IP: "enabling", "active", "degraded", "disabling", "off", or "failed".
- `surcharge_percent` (Number) Percentage added to the instance's hourly price while Dynamic IP is enabled.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import Dynamic IP by the id of the instance it is enabled on.
terraform import pantechdynamics_dynamic_ip.worker vm_06gge49p4ss4f1qkg5tewd0c2m
```
